Class SocketVirtualView

java.lang.Object
network.server.socket.SocketVirtualView
All Implemented Interfaces:
VirtualView
public class SocketVirtualView extends Object implements VirtualView
Server-side view of a socket client. Its sole responsibility is to transmit to the client the messages the server hands it.

Every sendXxx is dispatched onto a dedicated single-thread executor per player, so the game-thread never blocks on the TCP write of a slow client, and outbound messages to a given client are never interleaved. The view does not know the LobbyManager; if a write fails it just closes the socket, and SocketClientHandler.run() notices it via EOF/SocketException on its read loop and triggers the disconnect pipeline (calling lobbyManager.onDisconnect in its finally).

  • Field Details

    • SEND_INTERVAL_MS

      private static final long SEND_INTERVAL_MS
      Server-side socket liveness intervals (milliseconds). Invariant: TIMEOUT_MS > 2 * SEND_INTERVAL_MS, to tolerate scheduling jitter and brief delays from large application messages occupying the sender. Worst-case detection time is TIMEOUT_MS + CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 20 s.

      public SocketVirtualView(String playerName, Socket socket, ObjectOutputStream out, LobbyManager lobbyManager)
      Creates the view, sets up the single-thread sender executor and initialises the LivenessSentinel (not started yet; call activateLiveness() when the connection is ready).

      playerName - the name that identifies this player on the server
      socket - the underlying TCP socket (closed on write failure or close())
      out - the object output stream to write messages to
      lobbyManager - the lobby manager to notify when a timeout is detected

    • rawSend

      private void rawSend(ServerMessage msg)
      Writes a message directly to the output stream on the caller's thread (always the sender executor). Resets the stream before each write to prevent stale object-graph caching. On any IOException, marks the view as closed, shuts down the executor and closes the socket so that SocketClientHandler's read loop detects the failure.
      Parameters:
      msg - the message to serialise and send
